cards.text: Friend, Judah's last two kings, Manasseh and his son Amon, both did evil in the sight of the LORD (2 Kings 21:2, 20). Now Amon's son Josiah takes the throne and reigns in Jerusalem thirty-one years (2 Kings 21:26). Here's the thing, though. This new king is YOUNG.

cards.question: Josiah is ___ years old when he becomes king of Judah.

cards.text: EIGHT years old, with a whole kingdom on his shoulders. At eight, the biggest decision I could handle would be chocolate chips or sprinkles, and I'd still need a nap after.

cards.question: Young King Josiah follows the evil ways of his father Amon.

cards.text: Josiah does what's right in the eyes of the LORD, walking in all the ways of his ancestor David without turning aside to the right or to the left. Eight years old and he NEVER swerves, and I wobble clean across my bakery just reaching for a cookie box.
Fast forward to the eighteenth year of his reign. King Josiah sends Shaphan, his scribe, up to the house of the LORD to see Hilkiah the high priest.

cards.question: What does King Josiah want Hilkiah the high priest to count?

answers.text: The money brought into the temple
The priests serving in the temple
The gold cups kept in the temple

cards.text: The doorkeepers collected that money from the people. Once it's counted, it goes to the supervisors over the work on the house of the LORD.

cards.question: Josiah says the money then goes to the carpenters, builders and masons. What are they doing at the house of the LORD?
The workmen use the money to buy ___ and dressed ___ for the repairs.
King Josiah orders the workers to account for every bit of money put into their hands.

cards.text: No accounting needed, because they work with integrity. Friend, I spent YEARS buried under receipts nobody needed in that junk drawer, and these workers don't even need ONE.

cards.question: Then Hilkiah the high priest tells Shaphan the scribe he's found something in the house of the LORD. What is it?

cards.text: Hilkiah gives it to Shaphan, who reads it. Found it IN the house of the LORD, which is like me tearing my whole bakery apart for my recipe book and finding it under my own apron.

cards.question: When Shaphan reports back to King Josiah, the first thing he brings up is the book Hilkiah found.

cards.text: Shaphan reports the money first, and THEN he says, "Hilkiah the priest has given me a book." That's like burying the biggest news of the year at the bottom of a group chat about the electric bill.

cards.question: Shaphan reads the Book of the Law in the presence of King Josiah. When Josiah hears its words, what does he do?

cards.text: Josiah's clothes are torn, and now the king starts making calls. He summons Hilkiah the priest, Shaphan the scribe, Shaphan's son Ahikam, Achbor son of Micaiah, and Asaiah the king's servant.

cards.question: King Josiah gives Hilkiah, Shaphan and the others a job about the book that's been found. What is it?

answers.text: Go and ask the LORD about it
Go and make copies of it
Go and read it to the people

cards.question: Josiah says the wrath of the LORD burns against them because their fathers did not obey the words of the book.

cards.text: Notice Josiah doesn't point fingers. He says the wrath burns against "us," and the king counts himself right in with everybody else.

cards.question: Hilkiah, Shaphan and the other men go to ask the LORD about the book. Who do they go to?

cards.text: Huldah is the wife of Shallum, the keeper of the wardrobe, and she lives in Jerusalem in the Second District. Five of the king's men walk up to her door, and I bet NOBODY wanted to be the one to knock.
Huldah answers with "This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says" and gives the LORD's message for the man who sent them.

cards.question: Through Huldah, the LORD says He is about to bring calamity on this place and on its people.
The LORD says calamity is coming on this place and its people. What reason does He give?

answers.text: They forsook Him for other gods
They let His temple fall apart
They lost the Book of the Law

cards.text: They burned incense to other gods, and the LORD says His wrath will be kindled against this place and will not be quenched. Friend, that's the kind of news that makes a whole kitchen go quiet.
But then the message turns. It starts with "But as for the king of Judah" and carries a word just for Josiah.

cards.question: The LORD says He has heard King Josiah. What did Josiah do when he heard the words of the book?
The LORD says that when Josiah heard what He spoke against this place, Josiah's heart was ___.
The LORD tells Josiah he will be gathered to his grave in ___.
The LORD says Josiah will see all the calamity come on this place with his own eyes.

cards.text: So the men bring Huldah's answer back to the king. And that's where we'll leave it for now, friend, because this young king's story is NOWHERE near done.

findings.problem: Stop 2 starts at 2 Kings 22:11, but the passage's next stretch starts at 2 Kings 22:12.

rule.text: Each stop covers the next stretch of the passage, in order, and gives its verse range.

findings.problem: The opening card has four sentences: "Friend, Judah's last two kings...", "Now Amon's son Josiah...", "Here's the thing, though." and "This new king is YOUNG."

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on.

findings.problem: The card cites 2 Kings 21:26 for Josiah reigning thirty-one years. 21:26 only says Josiah became king. The thirty-one years comes from 2 Kings 22:1.

rule.text: References. Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: The joke "At eight, the biggest decision I could handle..." gives Papa Dorin a childhood at age eight, complete with naps. That adds something new to his backstory. He started out as a stamper in a bakery bin.

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.

findings.problem: The card only repeats the age from card 2 ("EIGHT years old") and adds a joke. It tells no new part of the passage.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards.

findings.problem: "Eight years old and he NEVER swerves" ties 22:2 to age eight. 22:2 describes Josiah's reign as a whole and gives no age or time.

rule.text: Times stay true. No time in the text means none added.

findings.problem: The two right words could be swapped: "stone and dressed timber" is a real, sensible phrase. A baker could argue that putting stone in blank 1 and timber in blank 2 is right, but it would be marked wrong.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: The comparison "tearing my whole bakery apart for my recipe book" is about searching for something you lost. Hilkiah wasn't searching. The book turns up during temple repairs, and the text never says anyone was looking for it. The two actions don't match.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The card tells Shaphan reporting the money first (22:9) and then mentioning the book (22:10), but it cites only 2 Kings 22:10. It should cite 2 Kings 22:9-10.

rule.text: Cite exactly what the card uses. Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: "Notice Josiah doesn't point fingers" isn't true to the text. In 22:13 Josiah names a cause: "because our fathers have not obeyed the words of this book."

rule.text: Noticing: What he points out must be true.

findings.problem: The card names Shallum as the keeper of the wardrobe. The BSB wording ("Shallum son of Tikvah, the son of Harhas, the keeper of the wardrobe") leaves open whether the title belongs to Shallum or to Harhas.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.
